samples.summary: `buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` called without the newly-required `depth` argument (3 sites)
samples.evidence: The delta changed `buildRowNode(row: TableRow, depth: number)` and `buildCellNode(cell: TableCell, depth: number)` to take a *required* second parameter, but three pre-existing call sites still pass one argument: `buildRowNode(row)` (line 2775, insertTableRow), `buildCellNode(cells[r])` (line 2818, insertTableColumn) and `buildCellNode(cell)` (line 2858, updateTableCell). Each is a TypeScript `TS2554: Expected 2 arguments, but got 1` — and packages/frontend runs no `tsc` at all, so nothing in CI catches it. At runtime `depth` is `undefined`, which propagates to `buildBlockNode(b, undefined)` and re-triggers the `depth = 0` default, so the nesting counter silently restarts at zero for every row insert, column insert and cell update: a nested table written through these paths is never capped at its true document depth.

samples.summary: The write-side nesting cap only holds for full-document writes; every incremental insert path restarts `depth` at 0
samples.evidence: `buildBlockNode`'s cap is relative to the `depth` its caller supplies, but all incremental writers call it with the default 0: `insertBlocksAfter` (2371), `replaceBlock`-style edit at 1723, 2312, 2335, 2505, 2584. A paste or block insert of an N-deep table into a cell that already sits at depth 31 therefore writes a chain of 31+N tables into the CRDT — precisely the "model deeper than any reader materializes" state the delta's importer cap and `writeFullDocument` refusal exist to prevent. Consequences are not a crash (the layout caps itself in table-layout.ts:145) but permanently invisible content and a document that every later `writeFullDocument`/`setHeader`-treeless call now *throws* on (the new guard at 3260), i.e. an unrepairable doc.

samples.summary: `setHeader`/`setFooter` tree path rewrites the whole header/footer subtree from the truncated read model, bypassing the new refusal
samples.evidence: `writeFullDocument` now throws when the model reaches `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, documented as: rewriting from the truncated `getDocument()` model would turn a read-time truncation into a replicated *deletion* of a peer's rows. But the normal (tree-initialized) `setHeader` path at line 967 — and `setFooter` at 1008 — rebuild the entire header/footer node from `header.blocks`, which callers obtain from the truncated `getHeader()` read, and `tree.editByPath([0],[1], node)` replaces the old node wholesale. A table past the cap inside a header is written back with `rows: []` (buildBlockNode line 390) or with whatever the truncated read produced, deleting the peer's rows — the exact hazard the guard was added for, reachable on the common path the guard does not cover.

samples.summary: Budget exhaustion in `expandCellRangeForMerges` yields an under-expanded rectangle that feeds destructive merge operations, not only painting
samples.evidence: The new `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` doc comment frames the degraded outcome as "a merge at its edge paints short". But `computeTableMergeContext` (table-merge-context.ts:53) and the drag/shift-click paths (text-editor.ts:3967, 3991) feed the expanded rectangle into the actual merge command. A rectangle that stopped growing mid-fixed-point can cut through an existing merged cell, so the merge writes a table whose covered cells no longer have an owner. 1<<18 = 262144 is also consumed by the plain outer scan alone on a 512x512 rectangle, before any orphan backtracking.

samples.summary: Cycle guard returns `false` ("no movement") after the cursor has already been relocated by the previous frame
samples.evidence: `moveToNextCell` moves the cursor at line 6016 (`this.cursor.moveTo({ blockId: parentCell.blocks[0].id, ... })`) *before* recursing. When the recursion's guard at 6014 (and 6078 in `moveToPrevCell`) detects the cycle it returns `false`, but the cursor has already been left on some ancestor cell's first block. Callers read `false` as "nothing happened": text-editor.ts:3088/3063 fall through to other arrow handling with a cursor that silently jumped, and text-editor.ts:2733 (Tab) clears the selection regardless. The documented contract "the caller reads it as no movement" does not hold.

samples.summary: `normalizeYsonTreeNode`'s recursion is bounded only by `row` nodes, so non-`row` nesting still overflows the stack
samples.evidence: The guard increments `depth` only when `node.type === 'row'` and truncates only row children. A snapshot containing an arbitrarily deep chain of any other node type (e.g. `cell > cell > cell > …`, or `block > block > …`, which nothing validates on the Yorkie tree) recurses unbounded in this function. The stated purpose of the cap is to keep this pre-reader walk from overflowing before `docsTreeToDocument`'s own cap applies; `docsTreeToDocument` never descends such chains (it filters by node type), so this normalizer is the only place they can blow the stack. Secondarily, a stray `row` node outside a table over-counts depth and truncates rows the reader would have read.

finding.summary: `buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` called without the newly-required `depth` argument (3 sites)
finding.evidence: The delta changed `buildRowNode(row: TableRow, depth: number)` and `buildCellNode(cell: TableCell, depth: number)` to take a *required* second parameter, but three pre-existing call sites still pass one argument: `buildRowNode(row)` (line 2775, insertTableRow), `buildCellNode(cells[r])` (line 2818, insertTableColumn) and `buildCellNode(cell)` (line 2858, updateTableCell). Each is a TypeScript `TS2554: Expected 2 arguments, but got 1` — and packages/frontend runs no `tsc` at all, so nothing in CI catches it. At runtime `depth` is `undefined`, which propagates to `buildBlockNode(b, undefined)` and re-triggers the `depth = 0` default, so the nesting counter silently restarts at zero for every row insert, column insert and cell update: a nested table written through these paths is never capped at its true document depth.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `buildCellNode(cell: TableCell, depth: number)` (line 417) and `buildRowNode(row: TableRow, depth: number)` (line 425) both take a required second parameter, yet three reachable call sites pass only one argument: `buildRowNode(row)` at line 2775 (insertTableRow), `buildCellNode(cells[r])` at line 2818 (insertTableColumn), and `buildCellNode(cell)` at line 2858 (updateTableCell). At runtime `depth` is `undefined`, which flows into `buildBlockNode(b, depth)` (line 421) where the `depth = 0` default (line 378) re-engages, and the cap check `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (line 390) is false for `undefined` on that first call — so the nesting counter silently restarts at zero on every row insert, column insert and cell update. That breaks the write-side invariant the surrounding code (lines 449, 523, 3268) exists to maintain: content can be written deeper than the reader's cap, producing rows the reader will silently drop. These are ordinary public store methods invoked by normal table editing, not defensive branches. packages/frontend/package.json has no typecheck script (build is plain `vite build`), so the TS2554 does not fail loudly in this package. No guard or caller re-supplies depth. Broken invariant plus silent data truncation on a normally reachable path — squarely in the correctness lane and at least major.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `buildBlockNode` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:378) caps table rows only at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (390-392), and depth only grows via buildRowNode/buildCellNode (421,429). All incremental writers call it with the default 0: updateBlock 1723, insertBlock 2312, insertBlockAfter 2335, insertBlocksAfter 2371, splitBlock 2505 and 2584 — exactly as claimed. These are cell-aware inserts (resolveBlockTreePath/getBlocksArrayForPath at 2322,2339,2366,2383), and paste into a cell routes there (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4567-4572 for a single table, 4641-4659 for multi-block; document.ts:783-788, 885-895). I found no nesting-depth guard on any insert path — `hasTableAtNestingCap` (446-457) is consulted only inside `writeFullDocument` (3260-3271). So an N-deep table inserted into a cell already near the cap writes a chain past the cap: the reader returns such a table with `rows: []` but with `tableData` present (509-552), making `hasTableAtNestingCap` true thereafter, so every later full write — setHeader 954, setFooter 993, setDocument 1039 — throws. Content permanently invisible and full-write paths permanently broken: a real correctness/invariant defect in my lane, not refutable as not-present, guarded, or out-of-scope.
